newsitem.title: USA: American Home to buy rest of Genetics.
newsitem.headline: American Home to buy rest of Genetics.

text.p: American Home Products Corp. said Tuesday it was exercising an option to buy the 40 percent of Genetics Institute Inc. it does not already own for about $1 billion.

The move by Madison, N.J.-based American Home comes less than a week after a Food and Drug Administration advisory panel voted to recommend approval of Genetics Institute's blood clotting therapy, known as BeneFix, for haemophilia B.

American Home Products, the maker of Advil and Anacin pain killers, Robitussin cough remedies and a host of prescription drugs, bought 60 percent of Genetics Institute in 1992. At the time it also received an option to acquire the rest.
Genetics Institute, a Cambridge, Mass.-based biotechnology company, develops drugs through recombinant DNA and other methods.

American Home said it would take a $700 million writeoff this year for purchased research and development and $300 million will be written off as goodwill. The charges will offset the gain to be reflected in the fourth quarter related to the sale of an 80 percent interest in American Home's food products business.
American Home's option to buy the rest of Genetics Institute escalated to the current exercise price of $85 a share.
Genetics Institute's stock rose $1.75 to $61.75 on Nasdaq.
